text: That is what the public sees and they use their SkillsFuture Credit to pay the last $100.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Excluding areas, such as safety, security and food and beverage (F&B), which produce a large number of training places partly because of regulations, the top nine areas today account for over half of the training places supported by SSG.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: They are ICT, service excellence, education and training, HR management, personal development, leadership and people management, business management, productivity and innovation and healthcare.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We did not plan for these numbers, but what we have designed is to allow the training industry and market to respond, and we provide support where we think the quality of training is good and it is aligned with our growth strategies.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Over time, many members of the public, and also Members of this House, such as Mr Low Thia Khiang, Assoc Prof Daniel Goh and Miss Cheng Li Hui, have asked for more demand-side support, such as study loans or tops-up of SkillsFuture Credit, for vulnerable workers or for mommies.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I agree that we should extend more help to these groups, especially if they are vulnerable.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Short courses often 90% to 95% subsidised, through supply-side funding.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: For someone taking a Diploma programme in a polytechnic or a Degree programme in an AU, study loans and tuition fee loans provided by the institutions are available to them.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Maybe this is not well-known by them, but even if you are an adult worker taking a part-time Degree or polytechnic courses, the loans are available to them.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Hence, the CPF Education scheme is only one option.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: For a back-to-work woman, besides course fee funding, she may need career support and job placement support.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: That is why we set up intermediaries, such as Community Development Councils (CDCs) and the Employment and Employability Institute (e2i).

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: They will help her access all the supply-side assistance out there, provide additional funding support if need be, and facilitate her job search and placement.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This is how we link training and employability, which Ms Foo Mee Har spoke about.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Similarly, training programmes developed under SkillsFuture supply the tools to MOM to implement Place and Train, Adapt and Grow, and Attach and Train, to help more targeted clients.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: And with the intermediaries, we bridge the gap between demand and supply-side support, such that workers can get individualised help, but not a customised grant.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Mr Ang Wei Neng asked if we can provide more financial support for our students in PSEIs, particularly in the universities.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This is one area of demand-side support that can be improved.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: And Minister Heng spoke about this in the Budget Statement.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: There are currently three bursary tiers for undergraduate and Diploma students from families with monthly household per capita incomes of $950 and below, $951 to $1,400, and $1,401 to $1,900.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: For ITE students, we provide additional assistance to students from families with a per capita income of $570 and below.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: So, three tiers for most but, for ITE students, four tiers.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This will allow us to be even more targeted in helping students from lower- to middle-income households.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: To be eligible for the bursary, a student only needs to meet either of the two income criteria.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Third, we will update the income eligibility caps based on the latest household income data.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Essentially, they will all be revised upwards and more students will qualify.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This will bring the maximum annual bursary quantum to $4,000 for undergraduates, $2,350 for diploma students, and $1,400 for ITE students.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: MOE will provide the details in a press release later today.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The total annual budget is estimated to increase by $50 million a year to $150 million a year.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Having built the infrastructure to support Lifelong Learning, we need to configure it, make sure we have the right approaches, policies, programmes and processes.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We are doing this actively, through the SkillsFuture Movement launched two years ago.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: ITEs, polytechnics and universities have, therefore, been revamping and improving their programmes.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: There is now great emphasis on industry attachment and internship.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: They are championing overseas internships so that students get early exposure to an international working environment, which Mr Zainal Sapari spoke about.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: NUS and NTU both run overseas entrepreneurship programmes where students are attached to startups and tech companies in Silicon Valley, China and Europe.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I was recently in Beijing, China, for the Joint Council for Bilateral Cooperation (JCBC).

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: During a dialogue with Singaporeans based there, I was pleasantly surprised to meet a big group of students from our universities, all on tech company attachments.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: SMU has introduced SMU-X, an initiative where students get to work on real-life industry problems, side by side with businesses.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: UniSIM and NTU are converting all their teaching materials for online delivery, to refresh their teaching methods and also to inoculate themselves against possible disruption in future.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: All over the system now, there is much greater emphasis on interdisciplinary teaching and studies.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But one critical configuration that we need to do is to ensure that our system takes into account the interests and aptitudes of our students.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This is because we are simply better at doing what we like.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Notwithstanding this, many of our youths go with the flow.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: They go into courses where their grades can take them or where their friends are going.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Our young need guidance and help to discover themselves, to discover their strengths and interests.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We need to strengthen our Education and Career Guidance in our education system considerably, starting from secondary schools.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Parliamentary Secretary Ms Low Yen Ling will speak more about this later.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But for those who are clear about what they want to pursue, we should support them as much as possible, to facilitate their admission into our PSEIs based on interests and aptitudes and not just based on academic results.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Dr Lim Wee Kiak and Mr Ang Wei Neng have asked how we can strengthen this.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The universities will be expanding aptitude-based admissions in their admission exercises later this year for up to 15% of their intake.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This was what I announced last year but they are implementing it for the academic year this year.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Some, however, like SIT and SMU, have been practising aptitude-based admissions on a fairly large scale and over many years.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: As for the polytechnics, since my announcement last year, they have implemented aptitude-based admissions through the Polytechnic Early Admissions Exercise (EAE) last year and the outcomes are encouraging.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: They received applications from about 8,000 O-level students, of which 2,500 successful applicants eventually had their EAE offers confirmed.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The eventual EAE intake is close to 12% of the total polytechnic intake, with two polytechnics bursting their 12.5% quota very slightly.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: And these are healthy utilisation rates for a first exercise.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: And, as expected, I got a lot more appeals this year.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Polytechnics have given feedback that EAE is particularly useful in sectors, such as social work, nursing, early childhood education or those that involve the creative arts, because your commitment and interest in the subject are very important for these courses.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This will mean about 500 more places included under EAE.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: There is also scope to apply aptitude-based admissions at the ITEs.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Currently, at the Higher Nitec level, only 10 out of nearly 50 courses are open for enrolment based on aptitude and interest.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: There should really be more, given that ITE courses are vocational and very specialised in nature.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: ITE also has a Special College Admissions Scheme, but applicants are considered based on general talents like leadership and sports, and not so much on aptitude and interest.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Hence, today, only a very small percentage of ITE students are admitted to ITE based on course-specific aptitude and interest.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Like the polytechnic EAE, ITE EAE will be conducted before the release of N- and O-Level results.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: There is another important thing we can do for ITE students.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I mentioned "learning by doing" as a key shift in the way we deliver higher education.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Ms Foo Mee Har, Mr Thomas Chua and Mr Ang Wei Neng have urged industries and PSEIs to collaborate more closely to deliver education.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The ethos of "learning by doing" actually has been the strongest at ITE, because of its tradition of vocational education and a very highly practical curriculum.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Today, many ITE students aspire to progress to the polytechnics.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Indeed, every year, about a quarter of them manage to do so.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: However, while a polytechnic education is applied in nature, it is not quite "learning by doing" in the sense of an apprenticeship, like a European apprenticeship.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: An ITE student still needs to score quite a good grade point average (GPA) and demonstrates quite good academic abilities before a polytechnic will take him or her in.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But many ITE students are talented at using their hands and probably learn best by practising, by doing.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This is a more natural path for them to achieve mastery, across a range of areas.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: And over time, with skills mastery, they should also have a chance to move up to management positions if they so desire.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: If you meet the general managers (GMs), which I do from time to time, you will find that there are two kinds of GMs.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: One type of GM is those that take a degree in hotel management and they get parachuted into the hotel.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: After some management associate programmes, they rise up.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Another type of GM starts off as an apprentice in the kitchen, sometimes in the restaurant.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: And they move around different departments of the hotel, different operations and, over many years, they know the operations so well and they are so competent at it, they rise up and become GM.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Every course will be delivered in partnership with an employer.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: ITE students will be able to apply for them after they graduate with a Nitec or Higher Nitec or after a few years of working.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: For a start, we will introduce this pathway in sectors, such as Mechanical and Electrical Services Design and Supervision, Security Systems Engineering, Rehabilitation Therapy and Offshore and Marine.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: With this new pathway, ITE students need not see polytechnics as their only path for progression.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: They can advance through skills mastery and practice, by staying with ITE. "Learning by doing" will also apply to universities.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I recently visited the Singapore office of an American technology company.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It is a big office in the Mapletree Business Park along Alexandra Road.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The company believes in training Singaporeans to be competent working in digital and data-intense workplaces.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: And the training is not just for their own employees.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: They said it is for anyone who is interested because they say that it builds up the entire ecosystem that way.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: They run an intense eight-month, hands-on programme for fresh graduates to learn about data management and data analytics.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: And I was told everyone who graduated from that programme was immediately snapped up by the industry because that skillset is in such short supply in the industry.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I was impressed by this very enlightened approach.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: They think big and they think long term.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: They even have a global function in Singapore where they are looking for their next one billion customers.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Members of this House will know this company.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The immediate question that sprung to my mind was: if the data analytics programme is so effective, why can it not be part of our university education curriculum?

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Therefore, our AUs must also co-recreate programmes with industries and promote "learning by doing".

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: They are jointly developed and delivered in partnership with companies, such as Singtel and Standard Chartered.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I am glad that Government agencies are coming on board quite actively.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: They are also partnering the Cyber Security Agency of Singapore (CSA) and also the Defence Science and Technology Agency (DSTA) of the Ministry of Defence (MINDEF).

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We hope, over time, more will do so.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: In fact, one of the Government Ministries that is a pioneer in providing "learning by doing" training programmes is MOE.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: At NIE, you do not just study in the classroom, but you would also practise teaching through a practicum.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I hope that such programmes for "learning by doing" will proliferate across our university landscape.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The third phase of the transformation plan for higher education is scale.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Where we have reasonably built and configured the system, we are ready to scale so that we can create a widespread impact and benefit Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Scaling will help guide more Singaporeans in their training journey and career paths.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We will also make more online tools and resources available for Singaporeans to do the same and to search and apply for jobs as well.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This will be done through a portal called MySkillsFuture.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We will also use the MySkillsFuture portal to publish training outcomes for selected courses.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Individuals and trainees will get to rate the training programmes and help others make better training decisions.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: One of our key strengths as a society is that we have always been able to mobilise Singaporeans whenever it is necessary to reskill our workforce or adapt to a sea-change.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: For example, in the 1980s, we launched two programmes − Basic Education for Skills Training (BEST) and Worker Improvement through Secondary Education (WISE).

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Those were efforts to build up literacy and numeracy skills amongst our workforce.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Those were the essential skills at that time.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Around the same period, as part of the national computerisation efforts, the Labour Movement set up the National Trades Union Congress (NTUC) Computer Training Centre to raise basic IT literacy for workers.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: About 10 years ago, running up to the setup and development of the Integrated Resorts, we launched the WSQ Certified Service Professional programme, an intense five-day programme, to train people to raise their service awareness and service delivery, and we trained tens of thousands of workers at that time.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The time has come again for us to undertake such an exercise.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The workplace of the future will be different, with lots of use of IT, robotics and data.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Not all our workforce, not every worker, needs to be an IT expert or needs to have programming skills but everyone will need some basic working knowledge, such as an understanding of emerging technologies, their impact on your work, and an ability to interpret and use data.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We also need to be equipped with a mindset for change, innovation and resilience.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: If you are a sales manager, you must be comfortable with diving into your data to understand what is generating your sales − what segments of clients, which geography, what products.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: If you are a taxi driver, instead of driving around to try to pick up customers, you learn to use all the different apps to match supply and demand, and you go to where the customers are.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: If you are a char kway teow man, you would not have to fry electronic kway teow, but you should be able to take electronic payments and electronic orders.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This is the digital environment that we must all get used to working in.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The course will not be a long one.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I expect it to be one or two days.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We can also scale our efforts and make an impact through our PSEIs.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Our AUs, in particular, have done very well in international rankings, which we can all be proud of.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: However, these are rankings by private organisations, based on their own criteria.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: And I agree with Mr Ang Wei Neng that such rankings may not fully reflect the social and public missions of an AU.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I do worry that, over time, our universities may get into the game of chasing rankings at the expense of their public missions.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: MOE will work with our AUs to further sharpen and articulate the public objectives of our AUs and tie part of our resource allocation to the fulfilment of these objectives.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: There are three objectives which we would like AUs to focus on.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This includes "learning by doing", overseas exposure for students, and new methods to deliver lessons, including leveraging technology and e-learning.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: All the AUs have already set up their lifelong learning units.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: They now need to ramp up the programmes, especially the bite-sized modular ones.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This is not a matter of just modularising existing programmes.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The lifelong learning units ought to be like Skunkworks or innovation units, constantly coming up with new programmes in response to industrial needs and the latest developments and technology.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: As NTU's President Bertil Andersson always tells me, there are only two kinds of research in this world − applied research and not-yet applied research.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: He said all research must ultimately change lives for the better, whether it is creating new enterprises, new jobs, giving us new insights into policies or implementing new projects that strengthen competitiveness or improve lives.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Mr Pritam Singh asked how SSRC will spread its grant awards between the Humanities and Social Sciences.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: One of the priority themes of SSRC is "identities, social integration and resilience" and it is really a broad theme.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: And this study is not complete without a study of Southeast Asia − its history, languages, communities, literatures − for a Singapore identity is unintelligible without the cultural backdrop of Southeast Asia and the broader region.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: So, please be reassured that the Humanities will be part of SSRC.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Teaching, lifelong learning, impactful research − these are all areas that our AUs are already working hard on.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: With a stronger alignment of missions, objectives and resource allocation, I believe this will better position our AUs to fulfil the important roles that they have in shaping the future of Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: In carrying out this plan, what is the toughest challenge of all?

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It is changing mindsets − the "die die must do this way" kind of thinking.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: First of all, all of us − parents, students, educators − will need to move our focus away from a relentless pursuit of academic grades to the larger view of human development.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: As Minister Ng Chee Meng had said, it is about the joy of learning, entrepreneurial dare, moral grounding and holistic development.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It will not change overnight but we are making important adjustments, even at the school level, to catalyse this change.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Hire based on interest, skills and cultural fit, not just based on qualifications and grades.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Because MOE can say all we want about dialing back from an over-emphasis on academic grades, but our message will ring hollow unless employers demonstrate that good jobs need not necessarily come only from good grades.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Third, society needs to recognise and celebrate a wide range of successes, not just managers and leaders but also entrepreneurs, craftsmen, technicians, sportsmen, artists.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The university's mission at that time, if I may put it starkly, and at the risk of some caricature, was to make sure that we produced as many university graduates as possible to support our economic growth.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: That was a pragmatic generation, which had to fight for collective survival.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: They realised the importance and critical need for education and hoped that their children would achieve good grades and obtain good qualifications.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: And to a large extent, for this current generation of parents, many of them still think that way.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Make no mistake, our goal must be still to fit graduates to an economic purpose.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: No one wants graduates who come out of the university and cannot find jobs.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But in this new era, our children have new ideas, too.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: They do not want to be on a treadmill, constantly chasing after good grades.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But I am sure that when our children grow up and they become parents, they will believe in multiple paths towards success.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: They will want their children to go through an education system that recognises their individual strengths.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But by then, times will have changed further and their children will have different ideas and they will be saying that their parents have very fixed mindsets.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Every generation that comes of age will transform and remake the society it lives in.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: That is how we progress, and education is there to help us along.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: That is why MOE's mission is to mould the future of Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Today, perhaps, we are at the starting line of a time of change and transformation.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It is up to us today to create these multiple paths and new opportunities which will take us to many different places but arrive at a common future − a Singapore of many talents, on a united yet multifaceted journey of one people and one country.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We want to do this with strong partnerships with our parents, industry and the community.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh and Mr Edwin Tong asked about arts education and how we are supporting our creative arts graduates in preparing for and developing their careers.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The interest in arts education and the range of opportunities and support available have increased over time.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Last year, I shared that MOE was looking into the creative arts tertiary education sector to improve the current landscape so that our creative arts graduates are better prepared for their future careers.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We have been speaking to various stakeholders to understand the sector and look at the graduate employment outcomes of creative arts graduates, especially those from the Arts institutions (AIs), which include NAFA and LASALLE.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Our engagements highlighted that creative arts play a role in our economy within and beyond the creative industries.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Against this backdrop, the AIs have started several initiatives to support their students better.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: First, Education and Career Guidance efforts are being strengthened.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: At LASALLE, all students are required to take a curriculum vitae (CV) and Cover Letter Writing course, as well as courses on personal branding and managing freelance work or a small business.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Such programmes prepare students better for stepping into the working world.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Second, there are continued efforts to build stronger industry links to enrich the curriculum and to expand internship opportunities.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: NAFA has revamped its curriculum to include industry-based learning to provide authentic learning opportunities as well as links with relevant industries.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Third, there will be greater provision of modular and short courses to support lifelong learning.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This will make it more flexible and practical for industry professionals to return to the classroom for further learning to deepen their skills.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: NAFA, for example, has developed several short, specialised courses, such as the Certificates in Visual Merchandising and Fashion Business, based on industry feedback.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: These courses are aimed at broadening the design and business skills of creative professionals.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We recognise the special role played by the AIs in offering pathways for those with the interest and talent in the field.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Going forward, there is value in developing NAFA and LASALLE further into centres of excellence in creative arts education.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: It will include efforts to further enhance teaching quality, strengthen employment outcomes and ensure financial sustainability.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Each institution will move at its own pace to implement the roadmap.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Beyond the AIs, we do see many who pursue private degree programmes to fulfil their aspirations.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: As Dr Tan Wu Meng pointed out, there is concern about the employability of graduates from these programmes.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: When deciding to attend such programmes, we want students to be more informed and make wise choices.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Parents play an important role in partnering schools to support their children in developing their passions into strengths and reaching their fullest potential.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We agree with Mr Zainal Sapari and Mr Gan Thiam Poh that strong school-home-community partnerships lead to better student outcomes.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We are committed to fostering such strong partnerships, and our Parent Support Groups (PSGs) play a very crucial role in this.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: To support PSGs, we recently launched the "Parent Support Groups − A how-to-guide by parents for parents".

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: It was developed by our parent representatives from the COMmunity and Parents in Support of Schools (COMPASS) who wanted to help others in setting up and running PSGs effectively.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Besides parents, the community also has a role in enriching our children's educational experiences.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This can be seen in the efforts by the community to make our mother tongue languages come alive.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: (In Malay):   The Malay Language Learning and Promotion Committee (MLLPC) has organised programmes and developed resources to nurture students' love for the Malay language and appreciate the usefulness and relevance of the language in their everyday settings.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: One such resource for parents is the Nabil and Nabilah Reader Series for Primary 1 and Primary 2.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The Series has been well-received by parents like Ms Siti Shyamira, who uses the story books as part of her family bonding sessions for reading and inculcation of values, such as respect for others.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: MLLPC will continue to build upon such efforts and is developing two language apps to support parents in their children's learning of the Malay language at home.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: These apps are targeted at the primary and secondary school level.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Without the active involvement and collaboration of various community partners, the impact and reach of these events would be limited.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: As the Malay proverb goes, "Shoulder the heavy, carry the light".

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Industry partners like companies, trade and business associations are crucial links between students' interests and careers.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Last September, I visited the ECG Fair that you see on the slide here, held at Nanyang Polytechnic and attended by more than 3,600 Secondary 3 students.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: It was at this fair where industry representatives showcased their work.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Their sharing enabled the Secondary 3 students to better understand and appreciate the industries and what it takes to be part of it.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Like what Minister Ng Chee Meng and Minister Ong Ye Kung mentioned earlier in their speeches, parents play a vital role in their children's aspirations and career planning.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We hope they can become actively involved as coaches and guides along their children's journey.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: This booklet is designed for parents and it is called, "Journeying with Our Children, Achieving Their Aspirations".

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I encourage parents and students to read it not just once but many times, and they will have very different takeaways because it allows students to reflect on what are their strengths, interests and talents and use these to make an informed decision about their education pathways and also career choices.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: The booklet itself, as well as the Parent Engagement Sessions, are some of the ways that MOE partners parents to help them better understand their children's interests, talents, strengths and passions.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: These parenting skills can also improve their parent-child relationship and mutual understanding and, through it, set a solid foundation for life.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: There are more opportunities at the tertiary level.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We will certainly promote more interest in this area, especially in Malay, Tamil and Chinese.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We will certainly continue to work with our community partners to make MTLs come alive for students.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Produced in partnership with the Lee Kuan Yew Fund for Bilingualism, the show fosters deeper appreciation of the three MTLs by showcasing their use and relevance in daily life.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Our children can catch the show on air every afternoon, and parents, if you can catch the re-telecast with your kids, please watch it with your young children as well.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: It means "Let's Connect with Tamil!" Through drama and cultural activities, it will show families how Tamil is fun and easy to use at home.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Our new primary school curriculum makes the MTLs come alive by reflecting the rich cultures and languages in everyday settings which our children can relate to.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Lessons often reflect the cultural festivals and national events that they experience in the real world.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: So, they are motivated to relate about what they have learnt.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: (In Mandarin):   Bilingualism is a foundational aspect of our education system.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I agree with what Ms Tin Pei Ling has said.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Our MTLs are not only rich in literary and cultural value but are also useful and constantly evolving living languages.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Today's students are "digital natives" and we need to engage them in ways that are familiar and interesting to them.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Only then can they discover the beauty of the language and an innate desire to learn more about it.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We are working closely with the Committee to Promote Chinese Language Learning, the Lee Kuan Yew Fund for Bilingualism, other community partners and our media friends, to create this vibrant language ecosystem for students to love the language.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Learning our MTLs must start from young, so that the child is used to expressing their thoughts and experiences in their MTLs.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: There will be new elements to the competition this year, which includes Xinyao workshops, using Xinyao songs, such as the Singapore Pie, to expound on our Singapore story and our local cultural heritage.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We will also be working closely with the Singapore Chinese Cultural Centre to help our students better appreciate our local Chinese culture.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Our iMTL interactive platform and Xuele online portal are tools that parents can use to engage their children in learning Chinese in a fun way.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Speaking of parents, many of our parents have themselves gone through a bilingual education and are well-equipped to help their children to learn Chinese.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Parents should take advantage of this strength by speaking to their children in Chinese, listening to Chinese songs, reading Chinese literature or watching Chinese programmes on television together with their children.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Our MTLs are cultural assets that Singaporeans should treasure.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: They are the foundation supporting our creative innovations and helping us connect to the rest of the world.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We will need to master more languages to achieve the CFE's recommendations to internationalise our economy.

speaker: The Chairman
text: We have a bit of time for clarifications.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Grateful for all the plans the Ministry has shared.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: It looks like we are in good hands.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: A lot of the changes that are mentioned depend on mindset changes on the part of employers, families, parents and educators.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Is there an ITM for them as well?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: The second question has to do with DSA.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Is there merit also in the long term to spread the talents across schools, which is a better reflection of the microcosm of society?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: My last question is for Minister of State Dr Janil.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I know he has a big heart for special needs students.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: But my concerns about the gaps were not addressed and I would like to know what he feels about them and what can be done.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We cannot say that we are going to solve today's problems or improve today's system through a mindset change.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I do not think it works that way.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We have seen how mindsets have changed over 20 years, over one generation.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: This is something we have to continuously work towards.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: It is also not just a school, but a mindset leap into a different kind of school.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I do not think we can change it overnight.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Neither do we say, "Oh, the system is doing well, so, tweak around the edges".

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: As I have assured Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar just now, the very core must be founded on good character and values.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: So, our educators must continue to inculcate such values in our children.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: As we move forward, given the new opportunities and challenges, we should not focus on the mechanics of learning but, as I have said, inculcate in our kids the joy of learning, an internal engine with which they will keep learning, whether they are seven years old or 70 years old, so that they have this internal engine to guide them to learn new skills throughout their lives.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: In summary, I will tell Ms Denise Phua, I do envisage that our future educators will be able to nurture the drive of our children, assist in building their competencies and skills, but, most importantly, their strength of character to guide them to succeed in the future.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: When we put the different processes that I have articulated in place, I do expect that talents, like what I have seen in St Theresa's Convent where they are passionate in hockey.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: But first of all, as we have emphasised in our speeches, move away from the over-emphasis on academic results.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: If I could start with the premise that she has put forward that we have to find ways to improve the effectiveness of the educators and the people who are working with children with special needs.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: I would also suggest that everybody involved agrees on that − MOE, MSF, our VWOs, community partners and also the groups of therapists and other professionals working within the SPED space.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The issue then is how to achieve that.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: A specific academy is very bold and ambitious and, perhaps, there are several steps we need to consider first before we are in a position to be able to do something as bold and ambitious as that.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: I think it is worth studying and looking at.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: There are several lines that need to be blurred and it is reflective of the difficulty of making progress in terms of excellence within SPED.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Any jurisdiction around the world would have different models of education, policy and SPED delivery.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, to be absolutely sure that you are doing the right thing on the basis of somebody else's model, we have to do it on the basis of our own model.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: It is very difficult to delineate lines between professions.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Many of the professional responsibilities are shared across the therapists with the educators.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: There are lines that need to be blurred between mainstream education and SPED education, between employers and educators, between administrators and the professionals.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Some of these things require a sort of complex approach involving multiple agencies and stakeholders before we can even think about arriving at something singular, like a SPED Academy.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: But I want to reassure Ms Phua that all the stakeholders involved have the same intent, which is, how can we improve the professionalism and expertise, either from an educator or other professionals' point of view, that we bring to bear to deliver the best possible education for all children, including those with special needs?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: And that is so, and everybody involved would like for us to be as excellent as possible in delivering these services.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, we have the same intent, and we can explore the various modalities.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The Member's suggestion of some form of a centre of excellence around special education is a very good one.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We will look at how we can make that possible.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
text: Presently, I understand that those colleges have collaborated with foreign universities to offer design-related degree courses.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
text: My question is: will the Ministry consider allowing them to upgrade to become arts universities and offer degrees to their students?

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: I share the hope and aspiration highlighted by Mr Gan Thiam Poh.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: That is why in my speech, I shared that we are working with both of them on a road map to enhance the standards of their programmes and to better prepare their students for the workforce.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: I feel that if we succeed in this, we will be able to enrich the landscape for young Singaporeans who wish to pursue their interests in the creative arts at the degree level.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: This, in itself, in my view, will raise the overall image of the creative arts as a career.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: The first is, I am very heartened that MOE and the schools have a lot of initiatives to develop character and values amongst students.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: But we must recognise that it is not the sole responsibility of schools.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: Parents have an equally important, if not more important, role in this.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: Are there plans to increase parental involvement, for example, in outdoor learning, or even in community work, so that they are involved together with their children?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: The second question is on the technical diploma.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: Would the technical diploma programme consider taking in working adults who do not have formal certification and who may have probably not completed their secondary school education so they do not have GCE "O" or "N" Levels, but now they want to upgrade themselves so that they have better job prospects?

speaker: The Chairman
text: So, please keep your clarifications and responses short.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: In terms of getting parents involved, yes, through a few things.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: One, last year, the Values in Action (VIA) programme where we get kids to learn cleaning.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: In the middle of last year, we actually got them to bring little booklets home to do chores together with their parents so that the learning is not just in school, but also at home.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Outdoor learning and community work, yes, we are exploring how we can do that better.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: There is a second question, Madam, by Dr Intan.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: It is a little bit different from when we were growing up, where a form class and a teaching class is 40.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Today, even though administratively, we organise a class according to 40 students, we do many different forms of educating our kids.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: In subject-based banding, we also have pupils who will go into separate classes to learn.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: It is a little bit more dynamic and we do create many more pathways, even in the schools itself, for the kids to move around.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: Chairman, I would like to seek a clarification from the Minister of State regarding the after-school care service that is school-based.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: He mentioned that the current supply itself actually meets demand.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: But why are we still seeing so many parents coming to us?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: I take the Member's point that there are localised areas where there is a waiting time and we are trying our best to solve this.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: With regard to public communication on both the demand and supply side of skills upgrading courses that are available, does the Ministry have any plans to raise public awareness of some of these courses?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: The signature of SkillsFuture is so large that people do focus quite a lot on the courses that they can choose with their SkillsFuture credits, but on the supply side, are there any plans to raise awareness as well?

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I am really happy the Member realised the challenge because SkillsFuture Credit has generated so much excitement.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: On the supply side, one of the problems − and it is for a valid reason − is that we tend to work with partners, be it industry associations, e2i and NTUC and so we also let them brand it.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The programme is actually a SkillsFuture programme, but MOM takes it, brands it as PCP and delivers it to workers to help them convert their careers.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Individual implementation agencies have their own branding, but SkillsFuture is behind it.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, maybe we are a little bit like Intel.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: On the question of applying discretion to a child who has not met the cut-off points, I think the answer was that there is DSA available to the child.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But would the Minister agree that this issue of DSA, applying that context is actually quite different?

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Because a child may have missed the cut-off point for a number of reasons and the school may wish to take the child for any number of reasons, such as the child has got good service and leadership records in the school, such as the child may be a head prefect or vice head prefect, something which is not easily captured or there is no equivalent in the DSA system.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: But we must look at the Primary 6 Posting Exercise in totality, from DSA all the way to PSLE.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: For those leadership skills that we value, they could have the full discretion at the DSA stage for admissions.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: At the PSLE results stage, we need to ensure that our posting system is fair and transparent.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: If there is a consideration for such traits and skills that could have been demonstrated in DSA before, then it will lead to many, many permutations.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: We do all the different assessments of talents, skills, all the different areas that we want to nurture.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Once we have the PSLE results, we want a fair and transparent system to ensure all students are fairly posted.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: I refer to my cut on the education loan.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: I understand that there is the Tuition Fee Loan scheme by the public-funded institutions.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: Would the Minister not agree that there are courses that are offered not by public-funded institutions, for instance, a diploma in teaching of Chinese and translation offered by the Singapore Chinese Chamber of Commerce and Industry Institute of Business which costs about $5,000 to $6,000 and the Government loan will probably come in handy to encourage people to take up such courses that are relevant to their career?

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I think we support a programme, on the supply side, if it really does help the worker raise their skills, find better jobs or become more employable.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: If it does not, then we should avoid funding them.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We do get a fair amount of pressure, different people wanting different kinds of courses, even though we know that those courses are not so useful.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The pressure is always there, so we are quite selective.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But in this case, if it is really a useful course, we should look at whether we should subsidise it.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: And if we subsidise it, it becomes more affordable and then maybe we do not even need a loan.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: People do part-time Diplomas because they are also working at the same time and, therefore, they can afford the subsidised fee.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I would say, for this particular instance, we should look at whether we should subsidise it.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I would be happy to look at it.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi
text: How prepared are our Statutory Boards, Government-linked companies and Civil Service in embracing or recognising modular training or e-learning by new job entrants?

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi
text: The second question is with regards SkillsFuture Credit.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi
text: Have we done a gender-based analysis or properly analysed which are the courses that are predominantly taken by the female cohorts, compared to the male cohorts?

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi
text: The third question is: has the Ministry considered, in order to encourage more people to take up STEM courses, can we have a scholarship allocated for female students in the IHLs?

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: On Statutory Boards, many of them have come forward, as I have mentioned earlier, in providing "learning by doing" programmes.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: As to whether they will recognise modular training, I think we have to strike a balance.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: On one hand, we do not want Statutory Boards and employers to only look at formal qualifications.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We also want to look at the interests and skills of the person.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: On the other hand, we also cannot swing all the way to say that we accept every modular training and e-learning because there are so many.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We can learn a lot of things now just by watching YouTube videos, going on Coursera and Udemy.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, I think we need a balance point.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We want to move away from just purely looking at qualifications but not swing all the way.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Our women are capable of doing very well in a range of fields even though they have to manage family responsibilities and parental responsibilities.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
